title: Halloween: what does the Bible say?
opening_question: The Bible never names Halloween. What does it say about the things the day touches: witchcraft and spirits of the dead, darkness and light, special days, and fear? Read what the text says, and be fully persuaded in your own mind.

steps.question: Which practices does the LORD list in Deuteronomy 18, what does He call them, and does witchcraft come up again in the New Testament?

facts.text: The KJV "necromancer" is two Hebrew words: darash, "to seek or ask", and muth, "to die": one who asks of the dead. The BSB says "inquires of the dead".
"witch" in Deuteronomy 18:10 is kashaph: "to whisper a spell".
"witchcraft" in Galatians 5:20 is pharmakeia, the word behind "pharmacy": "magic". It stands in the list of the works of the flesh.

steps.question: Where should a people seek: to the dead, or to their God? And why did Saul die?

facts.text: "familiar spirits" is the Hebrew 'ob; Strong's gives "a necromancer" among its meanings.
The text says what comes after death: "it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment".
1 Chronicles 10:13 looks back on 1 Samuel 28: Saul "had put away those that had familiar spirits", yet he asked for "a woman that hath a familiar spirit" and went to her at Endor.

steps.question: What were we once, what are we now, and what does the text say to do with the unfruitful works of darkness? What did the believers at Ephesus do with their books?

facts.text: "reprove" in Ephesians 5:11 is elencho: "to confute, admonish". The BSB says "expose them".
"curious arts" in Acts 19:19 is periergos, "magic". The books they burned were counted at "fifty thousand pieces of silver".

steps.question: One man esteems one day above another, another esteems every day alike: what does the text say about special days, and how is each person to decide?

facts.text: "fully persuaded" in Romans 14:5 is plerophoreo: "completely assure (or convince)".
Outside history, not Scripture: the name Halloween comes from All Hallows' Eve, the evening before All Saints' Day (1 November) in the church calendar.

steps.question: Paul on things tied to idols: what does he say about knowledge, about the weaker brother, and about doing all to the glory of God?

facts.text: Paul: "we know that an idol is nothing in the world", yet "take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak".

"All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient"; "Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth". This is the closest Bible passage to taking part in something tied to another religion.

steps.question: Why does a Christian not have to fear the darkness? What did Christ do to the principalities and powers, and to him that had the power of death?

facts.text: "spoiled" in Colossians 2:15 is apekduomai: "despoil". The BSB says "disarmed".

steps.question: What does the light do in the darkness, what does Jesus call Himself, and what does He call those who follow Him?

facts.text: "comprehended" in John 1:5 is katalambano: "to take eagerly, i.e. seize". The BSB and the Ethiopian Canon say the darkness has not "overcome it".
"light" in John 8:12 and Matthew 5:14 is the same Greek word, phos.

steps.question: Living it out: on a night of costumes and darkness, what do these verses ask of a believer toward neighbours, children and anyone who knocks at the door?

facts.text: "Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good"; "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt".

remember.text: "all that do these things are an abomination unto the LORD" ... "should not a people seek unto their God?"
"now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light" ... "have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them"
"Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind" ... "do all to the glory of God"
"greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world"
"the light shineth in darkness" ... "Let your light so shine before men"
